[USER] The user has been struggling with noise and blur when shooting in the early morning or evening.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for low-light photography, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Understand your camera's limitations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Use a tripod to prevent camera shake.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Shoot in RAW for better editing capabilities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Optimize ISO, keeping it as low as possible (preferably 400 or below).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Choose a wide aperture (like f/1.4 or f/2.8).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Slow down shutter speed (around 1/30s to 1/15s).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Pay attention to white balance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Use built-in noise reduction features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Shoot in burst mode for better chances of sharp images.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Edit photos using software like Lightroom or Photoshop.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips for specific situations:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Early morning: Shoot during the "golden hour" (about 30 minutes after sunrise).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Evening: Shoot during the "blue hour" (about 30 minutes before sunset).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Indoor low light: Use available light sources and avoid flash.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Bonus tip: Practice regularly to improve skills.
